subject: Epsilon-v2 variant adoption: checklist, gaps, and next steps
messages:
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
Cc: 
Date: 2027-06-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Epsilon-v2 variant adoption: checklist, gaps, and next steps

Team —

Quick summary: QuantumLytics sent over Epsilon-v2 (their latest 8B sparse-variant) and we ran a short smoke eval. Attaching the eval summary and a compatibility matrix I pulled from the intake run. At first glance Epsilon-v2 gives ~18% token-cost reduction on our default sampling config and a modest latency improvement for short seqs, but there are a few gaps before we can consider rolling it into production routes.

What I need from each of you by EOD Tuesday (2027-06-02):
- Infrastructure (Vivek): Can this variant be hosted on our existing 2xA100 pools without changing the kernel chain? Any memory/regression risks for KV cache on longer chats?
- Serving/runtime (Dev): Are there changes to compilation flags, quantization profile, or attention kernels required? If so, estimate effort in engineer-days.
- Product/rdt (Grace): Which customer routes are priority candidates for a canary? Any roadmap conflicts if we lock this variant for Q3?

Attachments: epsilon-eval-summary.pdf, epsilon-compat-matrix.csv

I think a short sync on Wednesday to align the canary plan is useful but want scoping first.

Thanks,
Lauren
Lauren Bishop
Director, Product — Model Ops
Redwood Inference
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-06-01T11:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Epsilon-v2 variant adoption: checklist, gaps, and next steps

Lauren —

Thanks for the artifacts. High level notes from infra:
- Memory/placement: Epsilon-v2 has a larger embedding table footprint in the sparse-form; on 2xA100 we can host it but peak memory is ~7% higher than our baseline. That means multi-tenant packing margins shrink; recommend reserving a 10% headroom for the first few canaries.
- KV cache: no functional change to KV layout, but we saw ~5% higher cache churn in the short tests. If customers run sustained long-history chats (10k+ tokens) we should monitor GC and eviction metrics during canary.
- Fallback policy: We should set an automatic fallback to the current prod variant if p99 latency increases by >30ms for more than 3 minutes. Can we specify that in the canary playbook?

I attached a quick canary-metrics-template.xlsx with the baseline signals I'd want (p50/p95/p99 latency, cost-per-token, cache-eviction-rate, memory-pressure).

Vivek
VP, Serving Infra
From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-06-02T08:21:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Epsilon-v2 variant adoption: checklist, gaps, and next steps

Thanks — dug into the compat matrix and ran the model through our compile harness. Technical notes:
- Kernel path: Epsilon-v2 requires a slightly different attention scheduling for sparse heads. The runtime already has the hook but we need a new kernel selection rule (small code change; estimate 3 engineer-days including testing).
- Quantization: We can use our existing 4-bit profile but need to add a per-layer calibration pass for the sparse blocks (1 engineer-day).
- Regression risks: Risk vector is around deterministic sampling differences that can cause token mismatches in evals (not correctness issues, but diffs for QA). Recommend we include a forced-deterministic-run check in the canary to compare outputs on a fixed prompt set.

Proposed canary plan (short):
1) Build variant in staging with the kernel-rule toggle off (no traffic). Run deterministic runs on our regression suite.
2) Enable canary toggle and route 0.5% of traffic from low-risk routes (retention-async, embeddings-only workflows excluded).
3) Monitor the signals Vivek listed and have a 30-minute manual guard window before increasing to 2%.

I added the compile change to a short PR branch and linked the internal doc for the intake checklist: https://redwood-internal.company/docs/model-intake/epsilon-v2-checklist

-Dev
SRE / Serving Runtime
From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-06-03T09:33:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Epsilon-v2 variant adoption: checklist, gaps, and next steps

All —

This looks encouraging and low effort overall. A couple of product items to call out before we schedule a canary:
- Customer routing: I suggest we target two internal routes for the initial 0.5% canary — a) search-assist beta (low state, high QPS) and b) insights-batch (lower QPS, higher memory pressure). That will surface both latency and memory regressions.
- Roadmap impact: If we take Epsilon-v2 into dedicated routes for customers that opt-in, we should flag the SDK notes and changelog for the July release. I can owner a tiny doc for downstream PMs and CS.
- Metrics and success criteria: Agree with Vivek's template; add a quality signal: output-perplexity delta on the fixed prompt set and any deterministic token-diff rate >0.5% should be a hard stop.

If all good, I'll set up a 30-minute sync Wednesday (2027-06-04 10:00 PT) to finalize the canary configuration and rollout owner list.

Grace
Group Product Manager, Model Platform
From: Amelia Torres <amelia@quantumlytics.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Cc: QuantumLytics Platform Team <platform@quantumlytics.com>
Date: 2027-06-04T16:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Epsilon-v2 variant adoption: checklist, gaps, and next steps

Hi Lauren —

Thanks for the thoughtful run and detailed notes — really appreciate the thoroughness. The Epsilon team is happy to support the canary. A few asks from our side:
- Data residency: for any customer routes that require EU residency, we need to confirm your canary runs won't route EU data through non-EU hardware. Can you confirm?
- SLA and fallbacks: QuantumLytics will accept Redwood's standard variant fallback policy but would like the DocuSign for the variant-adoption addendum signed (link: https://docusign.com/qs/epsilon-adoption) before we enable production keys.

I'll be on the call Wednesday and can walk through any integration questions.

Best,
Amelia Torres
Partnerships, QuantumLytics
